question: What Laguna de Bay tributary names, localities, and basin identities can be reconciled from public LLDA pages and selected hydrologic profiles without treating watersheds as river routes?

sourceFindings.locator: About the lake; characteristics and tributary text
sourceFindings.finding: Reports about 100 rivers/streams and 22 significant river systems; explicitly names tributaries and places the Bay/Calo/Maitem rivers in Bay and Molawin/Dampalit/Pele rivers in Los Baños.

sourceFindings.locator: Laguna de Bay and its Tributaries
sourceFindings.finding: Reports 21 major tributary systems and a 3,820 km² watershed across portions of Laguna, Rizal, Cavite, Batangas, Quezon and Metro Manila.
Reports the LLDA administrative region as 3,880 km² and states it is substantially larger than the basin.
Indexes 24 sub-basin profiles; this is a catchment count, not a tributary-river count. The selected Los Baños PDF link returned 403.

sourceFindings.locator: Geographic Location; Administrative Boundary; Drainage Network
sourceFindings.finding: Accessible PDF names municipalities in the sub-basin and shows drainage-network content; printed UTM corner text and map images are not verified GIS polygons.

sourceFindings.locator: Geographic location; Administrative Boundary; Drainage Network
sourceFindings.finding: Accessible PDF describes the broader San Cristobal sub-basin/system across Laguna, Cavite and Batangas; it says six localities while listing seven and has area-total discrepancies.
Provides source context for selected systems including Cabuyao, Morong-Teresa, Sapang Baho and Sta. Cruz; it is explicitly selective, and some linked details are historical.

sourceFindings.locator: Laguna municipal directory; Bay and Los Baños
sourceFindings.finding: Used only to map the explicit LLDA municipality labels to PSA 10-digit codes 0403402000 and 0403411000.

method.counting: Kept source-defined units separate: approximately 100 rivers/streams and 22 significant river systems on the LLDA overview, 21 major tributary systems on a second LLDA page, and 24 sub-basins in the atlas. No count was reconciled into a complete inventory.
method.locality: Mapped only explicit Bay and Los Baños wording to PSA municipality codes. Enriched existing Bay River and Molawin Creek locality associations, and added Calo, Maitem, Dampalit, and Pele as source-named leads.
method.identity: Linked clear existing waterbody names only. Abbreviated Sta. Cruz, duplicate San Juan identities, ambiguous trailing text, and basin-to-channel identity remain held.
method.geometry: No geometry was extracted. PDF maps and coordinate-corner text are not accepted as a verified channel or basin polygon; datum/zone and transformation were not established.
method.biologicalEvidence: No fish, diet, current-presence, absence, catchability, legal rule, safety, or access claim was derived from water-quality or hydrology material.
method.rights: No local raw source files were retained and no item-specific open license or application redistribution approval was verified.

nextAction: Continue the accessible LLDA sub-basin profile sweep, keeping catchment identities separate from river channels; then seek fish records with item-level locality, taxonomic and reuse review. Revisit blocked PDFs only through normal public access or an authorized copy.
